Frequencies are interpreted modulo N. Finite geometric summation gives ∑_j ω^((k−ℓ)j) = N when k ≡ ℓ modulo N and 0 otherwise. Consequently, the inverse transformation is x_j = ∑_k x̂_k ω^(kj). Expanding the squared modulus using this orthogonality proves Parseval: ∑_j |x_j|² = N∑_k |x̂_k|². The same identity holds for any complex vector.\n\nDifference multiplier and spectrum. Let (Dx)_j = x_{j+1}−x_j. Cyclic reindexing gives (Dx)̂_k = (ω^k−1)x̂_k, with |ω^k−1|² = 2−2 cos(2πk/N) = 4 sin²(πk/N) =: λ_k. Thus M(x) = N∑_k |x̂_k|² and E(x) = N∑_k λ_k|x̂_k|². Equivalently, the cyclic Laplacian (Lx)_j = 2x_j−x_{j−1}−x_{j+1} satisfies L(ω^(kj))_j = λ_k(ω^(kj))_j and E(x) = ∑_j x_j(Lx)_j.\n\nMinimum. The mean-zero hypothesis is precisely x̂_0 = 0. For 1 ≤ k ≤ N−1, define d(k) = min(k,N−k). Then 1 ≤ d(k) ≤ floor(N/2) and λ_k = 4 sin²(πd(k)/N). Since sin²(t) is strictly increasing on [0,π/2], the minimum is λ_* = 4 sin²(π/N), attained exactly when d(k) = 1, namely k = 1 and k = N−1. These are distinct for every N ≥ 3; frequency −1 is simply N−1 modulo N. Therefore E(x) ≥ λ_*M(x). Equality holds exactly when every coefficient outside these two frequencies vanishes.\n\nReal equality space and optimality. Reality gives x̂_(N−k) = conjugate(x̂_k). Writing c = x̂_1, an equality vector is therefore x_j = cω^j + conjugate(c)ω^(−j) = A cos(2πj/N) + B sin(2πj/N), where A = 2 Re(c) and B = −2 Im(c). Conversely, every such vector is real, mean-zero, and supported on the minimizing frequencies. Write C_j = cos(2πj/N) and S_j = sin(2πj/N). Because N does not divide 2, geometric summation gives ∑_j ω^(2j) = 0. Double-angle identities yield ⟨C,C⟩ = ⟨S,S⟩ = N/2 and ⟨C,S⟩ = 0. For any even N ≥ 4, the Nyquist frequency k = N/2 is self-conjugate, its Fourier coefficient is real, and its vector is ((−1)^j)_j. Its eigenvalue 4 is strictly larger than λ_*, so it adds no equality direction.\n\nSpectral foundation. Fourier vectors are mutually orthogonal with squared norm N. Let H = span_R{C,S}; its orthogonal projection is Px = (2/N)⟨x,C⟩C + (2/N)⟨x,S⟩S. For mean-zero x, Parseval gives ‖x−Px‖² = N∑_{k∉{0,1,N−1}}|x̂_k|² and E−λ_*M = N∑_{k∉{0,1,N−1}}(λ_k−λ_*)|x̂_k|². For N ≥ 4, the smallest complementary eigenvalue is 4 sin²(2π/N), attained exactly at k = 2,N−2, which coincide only for N = 4. Its gap above λ_* is positive. For N = 3, both complementary sums are empty; there is no complementary eigenvalue.",

  ],
  "split_suggestion": [],
  "important_update": true
}
